title: The Kaaba and the Masjid al-Haram, Mecca
summary: The Kaaba is a cubical structure at the centre of the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca. It is the direction (qibla) towards which Muslims face in their daily prayers and the focus of the annual pilgrimage. Sources record several rebuildings, among them under Ibn al-Zubayr in 683–684 and, after floods, by the Ottoman sultan Murad IV in 1630–1631.

uncertainty.note: Start is the earliest dated rebuilding in the sources opened, by Ibn al-Zubayr (QNL: 64 AH/683 CE; Saudipedia: 684; Archnet: 65 AH). The sources say the structure is older than this and was rebuilt several times earlier (Archnet: it predates Islam), but they give no earlier year. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: During the revolution of Ibn al-Zubayr 64 AH/683 CE, the Holy Kaaba was demolished by catapults. The Sacred House was rebuilt with some modifications in size.
In 693, Caliph Abdualmalik Bin Marwan ordered al-Kaaba to be rebuilt on the original construction that Quraysh had built. It remained in this condition until 1631
Ottoman Sultan Murad IV ordered the reconstruction of the Kaaba in 1039 AH/1630 CE.
rebuilt multiple times, 685/65 AH, 693/74 AH, latest in 1631/1040 AH

where.historical_name: The Kaʿba (al-Kaaba al-Musharrafa), the cubical shrine at the centre of the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca; held by Ibn al-Zubayr, ruler of Mecca, at the 683–684 rebuilding, and under the Ottoman sultans at the 1630–1631 rebuilding (Archnet)

importance.justification: Saudipedia calls the Masjid al-Haram the holiest site on earth for Muslims, who orient themselves towards it in prayer; Archnet describes the Kaaba as the qibla and the destination of the hajj.

phases.description: Demolished and rebuilt by Ibn al-Zubayr (QNL: 64 AH/683 CE; Saudipedia: completed 684).
Caliph Abd al-Malik ordered it rebuilt on the construction that Quraysh had built (Saudipedia: 693; Archnet gives 692 in its text; QNL gives no year).
Rebuilt on the order of Ottoman Sultan Murad IV after floods damaged the walls (QNL: 1039 AH/1630 CE; Saudipedia: 1631; Archnet: 1629 and a 1631/1040 AH event).

Saudipedia says the Kaaba did not need to be demolished again, only repaired and renovated; QNL says the latest renovation, under King Fahd, changed the roof and repaired the walls (no year given in the pages opened). The sources date the structure back before 683 but not to a year, so the model has no earlier phase.

materials.material: large granite blocks on a marble base 25 cm high (Murad IV rebuilding)

reviewer_note: Sacred site; described neutrally. Shape block: Archnet calls it a cubical structure and gives only height and exterior plan. Height is the least sure figure: Archnet says 15 m with a 10.5 m by 12 m plan; other pages seen (Al Jazeera) say 13.1 m high, 12.8 m long and 11.03 m wide, and Saudipedia gives side lengths of 9.90 to 12.04 m with no height. Only the Archnet figures are used, so the three model values describe one structure. Dates differ by a year between sources (683/684/685; 692/693; 1629/1630/1631); start 683 is QNL's. Archnet could not be re-fetched by script (bot check) and was read in the browser pane.
